stories.title: DeepMind agents formally verified Signal's core crypto code
stories.plain: Google DeepMind used a team of AI agents to write machine-checked mathematical proofs that the code behind Signal's one-to-one encrypted chats keeps its security promises. The work took about four weeks; comparable verification has historically taken expert teams years.
stories.eng: AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework: models translate security goals into formal specifications that human experts review, then agents powered by Gemini Carbon write proofs in the Lean proof assistant, which mechanically checks every step. The proofs cover the compiled code down to machine instructions, not just the protocol design. The agents audited their own output and flagged about 1% of the codebase for a human second look.
specs: 1:1 chats: confidentiality, authentication, forward secrecy, post-compromise security
stories.point: The point: AI can now do the slow, expensive part of proving software correct, leaving humans to decide what "correct" means.
stories.means: Formal verification means proving, with math a computer checks, that code meets a precise specification; unlike testing, it covers every possible input. It has been reserved for small, critical systems because writing proofs by hand takes specialists years. Here agents wrote the proofs and Lean rejected any step that did not hold, so a model cannot bluff its way through. To show the system was not rubber-stamping, the team put two old, already-fixed Signal bugs back into an isolated copy, and it produced proofs that both versions were insecure. Group chats, multi-device sync and the full app were not covered, and most of the human effort went into writing the specifications.
stories.industry: It is the same pattern as the current era: many agents generate, a strict automatic checker filters. Verification is one of the few places where agent output can be trusted without a human reading every line, which makes it a natural target as AI writes more of the world's code. Google is open-sourcing the specifications and proofs.
stories.you: If you own security-critical code, the bottleneck is shifting from writing proofs to writing precise specifications, which is a skill worth learning. The published Lean specs show what a machine-checkable security property looks like. AlphaProof Code itself is not offered as a product yet.
terms: Formal verification
Proving with machine-checked math that code satisfies a specification for all inputs.
Lean
A programming language and proof assistant that checks every logical step of a proof.
Forward secrecy
If a key leaks today, previously sent messages stay unreadable.
stories.why: Signal CTO Ehren Kret welcomed the work, saying automated verification gives Signal more confidence in its privacy protections.

stories.title: Google agent teams design quantum programs proven correct in Lean
stories.plain: A Google team built a library of quantum programs inside the Lean proof assistant and let AI agents write new ones against formal specifications. The agents beat previous best results, by up to 290 times on quantum arithmetic.
stories.eng: Large quantum programs cannot be run on today's hardware or simulated classically, so the usual generate-and-test loop fails. The team makes both correctness and resource cost provable in Lean: agents write a program to a spec and the proof checker confirms it works and what it costs. Agent teams share results through wikis and hold organized "conferences" to exchange ideas.
stories.point: The point: proofs can replace experiments when the hardware to test on does not exist yet.
stories.means: AI-driven discovery usually works by generating a candidate, running it and keeping what scores best. That breaks for quantum algorithms, because classical computers can only evaluate them on small or restricted instances. Putting programs in Lean turns "does it work and how much does it cost" into a question a proof checker answers without running anything. The gains are against prior published constructions; cheaper algorithms bring forward the point at which a given quantum machine is useful for chemistry or fusion problems.
stories.industry: This is the second result in a week of AI improving on human-designed quantum circuits, after the QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic work. It also joins AlphaProof Code and the Fermat formalization in using Lean as the verifier for large agent teams. Labs increasingly treat verifiable domains as the place where agents produce new results.
stories.you: The wiki-plus-conference setup is a concrete coordination pattern for big agent teams: shared written memory instead of endless chat. If you build agent systems, the lesson is to find or build a checker that scores output without a human. This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed.
terms: Formal specification
A precise, machine-readable statement of what a program must do.
Resource cost
How many qubits and gates a quantum program needs, which decides whether hardware can run it.
stories.why: The authors argue that human and AI work under proof rigor can design algorithms that no current computer can yet test.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's fast, cheap model for agent work
stories.plain: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster, cheaper sibling of its frontier Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon models, tuned for coding and agent tasks. Google says it matches Argon on a broad intelligence index at a fraction of the price.
stories.eng: It takes 1M input tokens and can emit up to 1M output tokens, with four thinking levels (low, medium, high by default, and a new xhigh) and flat pricing across the full context. In Google's Antigravity, an orchestrator mixing Carbon and Hydrogen reached near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using about 24% less quota and finishing about 19% faster.
stories.point: The point: near-frontier quality at small-model prices makes it cheaper to run many agents, or to route easy steps away from expensive models.
stories.means: Labs ship large models for hard reasoning and small fast ones for volume. Agents call a model dozens or hundreds of times per task, so the speed and price of the cheaper model decide what is affordable to automate. Google reports Hydrogen at 51 on Artificial Analysis' index against 50 for Argon, and roughly triple 3.8 Flash's score on Terminal-Bench, a test of completing real tasks in a shell. All figures are Google-reported; independent results will follow.
stories.industry: Model routing, mixing a strong planner with a cheap worker, is becoming standard in agent harnesses, and Google published its own mixed-model numbers. Google also led with agent safety figures, such as 2.3x more resilience to indirect prompt injection, which shows where enterprise buyers' worries now sit.
stories.you: If you run agents on a frontier model, try routing routine steps (file edits, tool calls, summaries) to Hydrogen and measure cost per completed task. Flat pricing across 1M tokens matters if you load whole repos into context. It is available now in the Gemini API and AI Studio.
terms: Thinking level
A setting that trades extra reasoning time and tokens for better answers.
Model routing
Sending each step of a task to the cheapest model that can handle it.
Terminal-Bench
A benchmark where models must complete tasks in a real command-line environment.
stories.why: Free Gemini app users get Hydrogen through automatic model selection, and it is rolling into Search and Sheets.

stories.title: IBM's LLMON markup trains models to ignore injected instructions
stories.plain: IBM released two small experimental Granite models that read LLMON, a new markup that labels every part of a prompt as an instruction, data, a requirement and so on. Trained to follow only the instructions they are told to run, the models resisted prompt-injection attacks far better than models without it.
stories.eng: Structure is written with reserved special tokens rather than characters like braces or quotes, so text inside a document cannot fake structure. Each block gets an ID, and an exec block binds an instruction to specific data, like passing arguments to a function. Training re-serialized an instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON with unbound decoy instructions the model must ignore, then ran five GRPO stages and a DPO stage on about 1,000 pairs drawn from the model's own responses to injection attempts.
stories.point: The point: prompt injection may be fixable in the input format and training, not only with filters wrapped around the model.
stories.means: Prompt injection works because an LLM sees everything as one stream of text: a web page or email it reads can say "ignore previous instructions" and the model may obey. Chat templates separate who is speaking but not what each piece of text is for. LLMON gives the model a typed structure that content cannot forge, and trains it to treat only bound instructions as commands. IBM stresses this is learned behavior, not a guarantee, and adaptive attacks spread over many turns are not yet covered.
stories.industry: Injection is the main security blocker for agents that read email, browse or process documents; Gemini 4 Hydrogen's launch the same day also led with injection-resilience numbers. A structural fix that other vendors could adopt would change how agent tools pass data to models. IBM ships converters from JSON and support in its Mellea library.
stories.you: If you build RAG or agent pipelines, think of this as parameterized queries versus string concatenation, the fix for SQL injection, applied to prompts. You can test the previews on Hugging Face against your own injection cases, but do not rely on them in production yet.
terms: Prompt injection
Malicious instructions hidden in content a model reads, which it then follows.
Special tokens
Reserved vocabulary entries that normal text cannot produce, used to mark structure.
GRPO / DPO
Reinforcement and preference-tuning methods used after pretraining to shape behavior.
stories.why: Exact robustness percentages appear only in a chart in IBM's post; the relative figures above are IBM's own.
stories.source: IBM Granite, Hugging Face blog · 12 Nov

stories.title: Anthropic lets companies run Claude Managed Agents in-house
stories.plain: Anthropic opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents. Companies run the agent server, tool sandboxes and session history on their own infrastructure, while the Claude model still runs at Anthropic or a cloud provider.
stories.eng: A cma-server serves the Managed Agents API and runs the agent loop; separate workers execute shell and file tools inside customer sandboxes; agents, sessions and history persist in the customer's PostgreSQL 16+. Model calls go to the Claude API by default, or to Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry or a customer-run gateway. Each deployment serves one tenant at one trust level.
specs: Agent loop, sandboxes, sessions, memory stores
Claude API, Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, own gateway
Private beta via Anthropic account team
stories.point: The point: the agent harness, not just the model, is becoming something enterprises deploy and own, like a database.
stories.means: A managed agent service runs the loop that calls the model, executes tools and stores the history. For regulated companies, the sticking point was that this history (code, files, tool outputs) lived on the vendor's servers. Now that part runs in-house. But every model call still sends the full conversation, including tool results, to whichever provider you choose, so it is not air-gapped. Nothing migrates from the hosted service: agents, skills, credentials and memory must be recreated.
stories.industry: Agent platforms are splitting into model and harness, and vendors now compete on where the harness runs. Self-hosting answers the data-residency objections that slow enterprise agent adoption while keeping the model as the paid service.
stories.you: If compliance blocked hosted agents at your company, this changes the conversation: sandboxes and logs stay inside your perimeter. Budget for the operations work that comes with it: securing the server, retention and deletion (backups and volumes keep copies), and installing each release.
terms: Agent harness
The software around a model that runs the loop, calls tools and keeps state.
Sandbox
An isolated environment where an agent's shell and file commands run.
Single-tenant
One deployment serves one customer or trust level only.
stories.why: Anthropic says it has no remote access to a customer-run server or its logs.

stories.title: NTT's world model previews a robot's move before it acts
stories.plain: NTT built a model that generates a short video of what will happen for each action a robot is considering, then picks the one least likely to drop or topple things. In a shelf-loading test, success rose from 73.1% to 92.3%.
stories.eng: A "physics control adapter" added to a video-generation model estimates each object's position, orientation, velocity and mass from video and steps them forward with equations of motion; the result guides the generated video so objects stop vanishing or deforming. Candidate actions from a VLA model or motion planner are each rolled out and scored for collapse, drops and collisions. It is built to run fast enough for existing control loops and outputs the physical quantities behind each prediction.
specs: OBJ3D, better LPIPS than prior methods
stories.point: The point: world models are starting to work as a safety check inside real robot control loops, not just as video demos.
stories.means: Video generators can imagine the future but often break physics: boxes melt or vanish mid-clip. That makes them useless for judging whether a stack will hold. NTT forces the imagined future to obey motion equations, so the robot can look ahead for each option and reject risky ones. The 19-point gain comes from a small robot simulating stacking, and NTT did not disclose trial sizes.
stories.industry: Learning how the world changes in response to actions is a leading candidate for what comes after text-only agents. This is a concrete industrial use: a verifier for a robot's policy, the same propose-and-check pattern that agent swarms use.
stories.you: If you work on robotics or simulation, the design is reusable: keep your policy model and add a predictive checker that scores candidate actions. Exposing physical quantities like mass and velocity makes the checker debuggable, unlike a black-box score.
terms: World model
A model that predicts how an environment will change when an agent acts.
VLA model
Vision-language-action model: turns camera input and instructions into robot motions.
LPIPS
A metric for how perceptually different two images are; lower is closer.
stories.why: Later targets include parcels, warehouses, manufacturing, construction and retail.

stories.title: Google and Samsung's Gemini glasses go on preorder from $395
stories.plain: Google and Samsung opened preorders for their first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Nine styles cost $395 to $489 and ship on 10 December.
stories.eng: Each pair weighs about 41 g and uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 with a 12 MP camera and up to nine hours of battery; it pairs with iPhones and some Pixel and Galaxy phones. Saying "Hey Gemini" lets you ask about what you are looking at, with live translation, walking directions, music and calls.
stories.point: The point: multimodal assistants are moving from the phone to a camera on your face, and bystander privacy is now part of the product spec.
stories.means: AI glasses are a camera, microphones and speakers wired to a multimodal model: you look at something and ask about it. Meta has dominated, shipping 81% of AI glasses in the first half of the year. Google's version builds in bystander protections: the camera stops if its recording light is covered, and faces are blurred before Gemini sees an image. Buyers must be 18 or older and agree not to film people without permission, or the glasses can be disabled.
stories.industry: Glasses are the main hardware bet for always-available AI. They turn low-latency multimodal inference and the privacy of people being filmed into product problems rather than research ones.
stories.you: If you build mobile or multimodal apps, plan for a "what am I looking at" input mode with short spoken answers. Blurring faces before an image reaches the model is a pattern worth copying in any camera pipeline that calls an LLM.
terms: Multimodal model
A model that takes images, audio and text together.
Snapdragon AR1
Qualcomm's low-power chip designed for camera-equipped smart glasses.
stories.why: Warby Parker styles launch in the US only; Gentle Monster styles also go on sale in South Korea.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress steps in
stories.plain: Nvidia's board said Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director, effective immediately, after 33 years leading the company. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent successor.
stories.eng: The board's SEC filing gives no reason. It follows reports about Huang's personal relationships and a security investigation; those remain allegations, and Nvidia says it found no evidence that corporate or national-security secrets were compromised. Harvey C. Jones becomes Nvidia's first-ever board chair, and the search covers internal and external candidates.
stories.point: The point: the company supplying most of the world's AI compute just lost the founder who set its strategy, days before earnings.
stories.means: Nvidia's GPUs and CUDA software run most AI training and inference, and Huang personally drove its product bets, investments and partnerships. The board says the roadmap and customer commitments continue without interruption. Semafor argues AI companies may no longer count on Nvidia backing the market on the same terms, since Nvidia has invested in many of its own customers, including a stake in Anthropic's IPO private placement.
stories.industry: Nvidia is supplier and investor across the AI stack, from cloud providers to labs. Leadership uncertainty could touch deal-making, export-policy talks between the US and China, and pending acquisitions such as Hugging Face.
stories.you: Day to day, nothing changes for CUDA, drivers or hardware roadmaps. Watch the 17 November earnings call for any change in supply, pricing or the open-source commitments around Hugging Face.
terms: The SEC filing US public companies use to report major events such as a CEO change.
Interim CEO
A temporary chief executive who serves until a permanent one is named.
stories.why: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue pledged to keep defending open-source AI after Huang's exit.

stories.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed Notion AI chat transcripts
stories.plain: Fireworks AI, a platform that serves open models to developers, confirmed attackers reached customer data through its cloud provider. Notion said chat transcripts from some Notion AI users were taken, affecting around 1% of its customers.
stories.eng: Attackers breached Fireworks' cloud provider to reach a Fireworks development system, then took billing information and some customer datasets. Notion's stolen data covers model inputs and outputs written to chat in its Insights feature, much of it not attributable to a specific customer. Fireworks says the attackers aim to resell stolen access to language models.
specs: Disconnected and deleted data on 3 Nov
Fireworks' second breach in two months
stories.point: The point: your AI vendor's inference provider is part of your attack surface, and prompts and outputs are sensitive data.
stories.means: Many AI features sit on a chain of vendors: an app calls a model host, which runs on a cloud. Prompts and outputs pass through, and are sometimes stored at, each link. Here a breach two layers down exposed what users typed into Notion AI. The attackers' main goal was not the data but free compute: stolen access lets them sell model usage to others, a practice known as LLMjacking.
stories.industry: As companies route traffic through hosted platforms for open models, those platforms become high-value targets. Expect closer scrutiny of data retention, sub-processor lists and credential security in AI vendor contracts.
stories.you: Map where your prompts and completions go, including your vendors' vendors, and whether any of it is stored. Rotate model API keys, set spending limits and alert on unusual usage, which is how LLMjacking is usually caught.
terms: LLMjacking
Stealing credentials or access to AI models and reselling or abusing the compute.
Sub-processor
A third party your vendor uses to process your data.
stories.why: Fireworks says it serves tens of thousands of customers, including Harvey and Cursor; no other affected customers were named.

stories.title: New York opens AI safety registry; frontier labs must sign up
stories.plain: New York opened registration under its RAISE Act, which requires large AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic to publish safety frameworks and report serious incidents. They must register by 1 January 2027, when the law takes effect.
stories.eng: The law covers frontier developers with more than $500M in annual revenue. They must publish a safety framework, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, issue model transparency reports and register with the state. A new Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity and Trust (DIGIT) enforces it, working with a new SUNY Binghamton center that will evaluate advanced models.
specs: NY Center for AI Responsibility and Research
stories.point: The point: US frontier AI rules are being written state by state, and New York now sets the tightest reporting clock.
stories.means: With no federal AI law, states are writing their own rules for the biggest labs. California's SB 53 took effect in January 2026; New York's law is similar but demands incident reports within 72 hours instead of 15 days. Illinois' SB 315, also effective in 2027, adds independent safety audits. These rules require disclosure and reporting; they do not restrict what models can do.
stories.industry: Labs now juggle overlapping state regimes, which strengthens the push in Congress for a federal framework that would override them. Short reporting deadlines also force companies to build monitoring that catches serious failures fast.
stories.you: If you build on a covered lab's models, expect more published safety frameworks and transparency reports you can cite in your own risk reviews. Smaller companies fall below the threshold, but enterprise customers may start asking for similar documentation.
terms: Frontier developer
Here, a company training advanced models with over $500M in annual revenue.
Safety framework
A public document describing how a lab tests for and limits severe risks.
Preemption
A federal law overriding state laws on the same subject.
stories.why: The SUNY Binghamton center, announced in January with $55 million in donations and capital, launched the same day.

concepts.name: Agents that prove code correct
concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.
signals: 10 Nov
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's one-to-one crypto down to machine instructions; humans review ~1% of the code.

~1,000 Claude agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in about 30 hours.

Google builds a Lean library where agents write quantum programs whose correctness and cost are proven.

concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.

Three-part agent memory architecture lifts Opus 5.5 on CL-Bench from 0.644 to 0.833.

concepts.name: Continual world models
concepts.desc: Models that learn physics and causality from observation and keep updating after training. The bridge from text to physical tasks.

concepts.name: Instruction–data separation
concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
